figs.name: astable-vs-monostable-vs-bistable-multivibrator-identify-flowchart
figs.alt: flowchart to identify astable, monostable and bistable multivibrator circuits by stable states
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog showing a decision flowchart that identifies a multivibrator from its trigger and output behaviour, with typical uses of each type.
figs.after_h2: 4 Steps to Identify Which Circuit You Have
figs.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 560" width="100%" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif">
<title>Flowchart to identify an astable, monostable or bistable circuit</title>
<rect width="800" height="560" fill="#ffffff"/>
<defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0 0L10 5L0 10z" fill="#1a2b4a"/></marker></defs>
<text x="400.0" y="34" font-size="24" fill="#5b21b6" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Which Multivibrator Do You Have?</text>
<rect x="260" y="58" width="280" height="56" rx="10" fill="#f5f3ff" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="400.0" y="92.65" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Look at the output</text>
<line x1="400" y1="114" x2="400" y2="138" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<polygon points="400,140.0 540.0,192 400,244.0 260.0,192" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="400" y="187.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Toggles with no</text>
<text x="400" y="208.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">trigger input?</text>
<line x1="540" y1="192" x2="590" y2="192" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="565" y="182" font-size="17" fill="#5b21b6" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Yes</text>
<rect x="592" y="152" width="180" height="80" rx="10" fill="#ede9fe" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="682.0" y="186.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Astable</text>
<text x="682.0" y="209.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">zero stable states</text>
<line x1="400" y1="244" x2="400" y2="272" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="418" y="264" font-size="17" fill="#5b21b6" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">No</text>
<polygon points="400,274.0 540.0,326 400,378.0 260.0,326" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="400" y="321.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Returns to rest</text>
<text x="400" y="342.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">after fixed time?</text>
<line x1="540" y1="326" x2="590" y2="326" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="565" y="316" font-size="17" fill="#5b21b6" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Yes</text>
<rect x="592" y="286" width="180" height="80" rx="10" fill="#ede9fe" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="682.0" y="320.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Monostable</text>
<text x="682.0" y="343.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">one stable state</text>
<line x1="400" y1="378" x2="400" y2="406" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="418" y="398" font-size="17" fill="#5b21b6" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">No</text>
<polygon points="400,408.0 540.0,460 400,512.0 260.0,460" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="400" y="455.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Holds state until</text>
<text x="400" y="476.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">next trigger?</text>
<line x1="540" y1="460" x2="590" y2="460" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="565" y="450" font-size="17" fill="#5b21b6" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Yes</text>
<rect x="592" y="420" width="180" height="80" rx="10" fill="#ede9fe" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="682.0" y="454.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Bistable</text>
<text x="682.0" y="477.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">two stable states</text>
<rect x="30" y="170" width="190" height="300" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#5b21b6" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="125.0" y="199.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Uses</text>
<text x="125.0" y="222.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle"></text>
<text x="125.0" y="245.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Astable:</text>
<text x="125.0" y="268.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">clocks, tones</text>
<text x="125.0" y="291.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle"></text>
<text x="125.0" y="314.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Monostable:</text>
<text x="125.0" y="337.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">timing, delays,</text>
<text x="125.0" y="360.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">debounce</text>
<text x="125.0" y="383.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle"></text>
<text x="125.0" y="406.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Bistable:</text>
<text x="125.0" y="429.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">latches,</text>
<text x="125.0" y="452.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">flip flops</text>
<text x="400" y="540" font-size="18" fill="#4b5563" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Count the stable states: 0, 1 or 2</text>
</svg>

figs.name: astable-vs-monostable-vs-bistable-multivibrator-frequency-infographic
figs.alt: 555 astable frequency formula worked example with R1, R2 and C values
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog working the 555 astable formula f = 1.44 / ((R1 + 2R2) C) with 1 kilohm, 10 kilohm and 1 microfarad to get 68.6 Hz.
figs.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 500" width="100%" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif">
<title>555 astable frequency formula with worked example</title>
<rect width="800" height="500" fill="#ffffff"/>
<defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0 0L10 5L0 10z" fill="#1a2b4a"/></marker></defs>
<text x="400.0" y="34" font-size="24" fill="#5b21b6" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">555 Astable Frequency Formula</text>
<rect x="40" y="65" width="720" height="100" rx="14" fill="#7c3aed"/>
<text x="400" y="112" font-size="28" fill="#ffffff" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">f = 1.44 / ((R1 + 2 × R2) × C)</text>
<text x="400" y="148" font-size="18" fill="#ede9fe" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">charge through R1 + R2, discharge through R2</text>
<rect x="40" y="190" width="225" height="100" rx="12" fill="#f5f3ff" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="152" y="230" font-size="20" fill="#5b21b6" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">R1</text>
<text x="152" y="268" font-size="24" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">1 kΩ</text>
<rect x="285" y="190" width="225" height="100" rx="12" fill="#f5f3ff" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="397" y="230" font-size="20" fill="#5b21b6" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">R2</text>
<text x="397" y="268" font-size="24" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">10 kΩ</text>
<rect x="530" y="190" width="225" height="100" rx="12" fill="#f5f3ff" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="642" y="230" font-size="20" fill="#5b21b6" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">C</text>
<text x="642" y="268" font-size="24" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">1 µF</text>
<text x="60" y="335" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">Step 1:  R1 + 2 × R2 = 1 kΩ + 20 kΩ = 21 kΩ</text>
<text x="60" y="370" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">Step 2:  21000 Ω × 0.000001 F = 0.021 s</text>
<text x="60" y="405" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">Step 3:  f = 1.44 / 0.021</text>
<rect x="500" y="355" width="260" height="70" rx="12" fill="#ede9fe" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<text x="630" y="400" font-size="26" fill="#5b21b6" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">f = 68.6 Hz</text>
<text x="400" y="470" font-size="18" fill="#4b5563" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Five or ten percent part tolerance shifts the real frequency</text>
</svg>
